title: Wipro Appoints Former Macy's Tech Leader Laura Miller to Board of Directors
excerpt: Miller, who shaped digital and AI strategy at Macy's and holds board seats at NCR Voyix and Ahold Delhaize, joins Wipro for a five-year term effective April 2026.
body:
• Wipro has appointed Laura Marie Miller as an independent director for a five-year term beginning April 1, 2026, subject to shareholder approval.
  • Miller brings over 20 years of executive experience, including a key role shaping digital and AI strategy at Macy's.
  • She becomes the 10th member of Wipro's board, joining alongside chairman Rishad Premji and CEO Srini Pallia.

Wipro Limited, the Bengaluru-headquartered IT services and consulting company, has appointed Laura Marie Miller to its board of directors as an independent director. Her five-year term takes effect from April 1, 2026, pending shareholder approval, which was subsequently secured through a postal ballot in May with 99.81 per cent votes in favour.

A Career Spanning Retail, Hospitality, and Payments

Miller brings more than two decades of executive leadership experience to Wipro, with a track record of steering large global organisations through digital transformation. She is widely recognised for aligning technology and data capabilities with business strategy to drive long-term growth.

Her most prominent role was as a member of the executive leadership team at Macy's, the American department store chain, where she played a central part in developing the company's digital, data, and AI strategy. Before Macy's, she held global leadership positions at InterContinental Hotels Group and First Data (now Fiserv), working closely with boards and executive teams during periods of organisational change.

"Laura is a proven technology leader with deep experience guiding global organisations through complex change. Her strategic leadership, public company board experience, and understanding of technology governance and risk make her a valuable addition to our Board."

— Rishad Premji, Executive Chairman, Wipro Limited

Extensive Boardroom Experience

Miller's credentials extend well beyond the C-suite. She previously served as a director at EVO Payments during a period of strong growth that culminated in its acquisition by Global Payments. She also sat on the board of LGI Homes, one of the largest homebuilders in the United States.

She currently holds non-executive director roles at two major public companies: NCR Voyix, the Atlanta-based digital commerce company, and Ahold Delhaize, the Dutch-Belgian retail giant that operates chains including Stop & Shop, Food Lion, and Albert Heijn.

Miller holds a Bachelor of Science in Information Systems Management from the University of Maryland, Baltimore County, and a Master of Science in Computer Systems Management from the University of Maryland, University College.

What It Means for Wipro

The appointment comes as Wipro, which trades on the NYSE under the ticker WIT, pushes deeper into AI-powered services. The company, which employs over 230,000 people across 65 countries, has positioned its Wipro Intelligence suite of AI platforms as central to its client offerings.

Miller's experience navigating AI-driven transformation at Macy's — a retailer that has aggressively adopted machine learning for inventory management, personalisation, and customer analytics — is directly relevant to the kind of advisory role Wipro's board requires as AI reshapes IT services delivery.

"I am honoured to join the Board of Wipro Limited at a time of profound change driven by AI and rapidly evolving technologies. I look forward to supporting the company's mission of helping clients translate innovation into meaningful and lasting business outcomes."

— Laura Miller, Independent Director, Wipro Limited

With Miller's addition, Wipro's board expands to 10 members. The board includes founder Azim Premji, Executive Chairman Rishad Premji, and CEO and Managing Director Srini Pallia. Based in East Brunswick, New Jersey — where Wipro maintains its Americas headquarters — and Bengaluru, Miller bridges the company's dual geography.

The Bigger Picture

The move fits a broader pattern among Indian IT majors — including Infosys, TCS, and HCLTech — of recruiting American corporate leaders with deep technology governance experience to their boards. As these firms compete for larger, more complex enterprise deals in North America and Europe, directors who understand both the buyer's boardroom and the regulatory landscape are increasingly prized.

For the Indian diaspora employed across Wipro's global operations, the appointment signals continued investment in leadership that reflects the company's international footprint.
